svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-mitigation-billing-floors; chapter number: 2; title: Mitigation Billing Floors Per Visit and Per Job; subtitle: Shane O'Dazier's street numbers for getting paid on water work; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: USD; bars: label: Initial Response Charge; min: 285; max: 285; typical: 285; display: $285 initial response; label: Minimum Per Truck Roll; min: 400; max: 500; typical: 400; display: At least $400-$500 every time the truck rolls; label: Truck Mount Uplift Per Job; min: 300; max: 400; typical: 300; display: $300-$400 added by billing $189-$289 per committed hour; label: Monitoring Trip Lump Charge; min: 150; max: 489; typical: 489; display: $489 per trip vs roughly $150 billed hourly; label: Small Cash-Pay Job Floor; min: 800; max: 2000; typical: 2000; display: $800-$1,000 in trips before work, so priced at $2,000; caption: Change your pricing, never your scope. A $489 assess-and-reposition trip sat on a $7,300 invoice that was paid in full.; assumptions note: Where a range was stated, the typical marker sits on the stated floor or the practitioner's own chosen price. No midpoints were calculated.; note: Attributed to Shane O'Dazier of RestorationProfits. ReconSmart Solutions pushes back that documentation, never a target dollar figure, drives the estimate.
